issues.t: Ignition switch can fail and cut power to accessories
issues.sym: Wipers, lights, turn signals or other accessories quit or act up with the key on, sometimes on and off.
issues.why: The ignition switch fitted to these cars could fail internally, so circuits that run through it lose power. Audi recalled the cars to replace the switch.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN for recall 96V-017. If accessories cut out while driving, get the switch replaced soon.

issues.t: Driver airbag can go off from a static shock
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In dry weather a static spark from the driver touching the wheel could fire the airbag.
issues.why: The steering wheel airbag circuit was not well grounded, so a static discharge could set off the igniter. The recall adds a ground wire.
issues.next: Check that recall 97V-175 was done. If it is still open, have it completed before driving the car regularly.

issues.t: Rear seat belts may not lock
issues.sym: A rear belt pulls out freely when tugged hard instead of catching, or does not hold a child seat tight.
issues.why: The rear belt retractors on some 1997 cars could fail to lock as designed. Audi recalled them to replace the rear belt assemblies.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 97V-115 and do not carry rear passengers on a belt that will not lock.

issues.t: Front tie rod ends can wear out early
issues.sym: Loose or wandering steering, a clunk from the front end over bumps, or uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: The seals on the outer tie rods could fail and let dirt and water into the joint, which then wears quickly. Audi recalled the cars to replace the tie rods.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 99V-248 and 00V-414. A loose tie rod can separate, so have looseness inspected right away.

issues.t: Throttle can stick open in extreme cold
issues.sym: In very cold weather the engine keeps revving or the car keeps pulling after you lift off the gas pedal.
issues.why: On automatic-transmission cars with the 2.8L V6, moisture could freeze inside the throttle body and hold it open. A recall fits a revised throttle body kit.
issues.next: If this happens, brake firmly, shift to neutral and stop safely. Check the VIN for recall 04V-495 before winter driving.

issues.t: Fuel gauge can read full when the tank is not
issues.sym: The gauge stays near full or reads higher than it should, and the car can run out of fuel without warning.
issues.why: Sulfur in gasoline can coat the contacts on the fuel level senders so they report the wrong level. Audi recalled the cars to fit senders made from a different alloy.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 01V-157. Until it is fixed, track your mileage per tank instead of trusting the gauge.

issues.t: Headlight switch wiring can short and overheat
issues.sym: Headlights flicker or go out, the switch area feels hot, or there is a burning smell or smoke near the driver knee area.
issues.why: The wiring behind the headlight switch can be rubbed by the driver knee or overloaded at the connector pins, causing a short. Two recalls add protection and a jumper harness.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 04V-133 and 06V-198. If you smell burning near the switch, stop driving and have it inspected because of the fire risk.

issues.t: Instrument cluster center display loses pixels
issues.sym: Lines or blank patches across the trip computer display between the gauges, or a display that is too dim to read.
issues.why: The small display in the cluster is known to fail with age. The gauges usually keep working, but messages and warnings on the screen become hard to read.
issues.next: Not urgent, but have the cluster repaired or the display replaced so you do not miss warning messages.

issues.t: Fuel tank vent valve can crack and leak fuel
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell around the rear of the car, especially after filling up, and sometimes a wet spot under the tank.
issues.why: A plastic nipple on the rollover valve at the top of the fuel tank can crack and let fuel escape. Recalls cover cars with every engine sold in these years.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 08V-157 and 11V-267. Leaking fuel is a fire risk, so have it looked at promptly and avoid topping off the tank.

issues.t: Fuel pump can quit and stall the engine
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or cranks without starting, often with no warning beforehand.
issues.why: A change to the fuel pump motor on cars built from late 2002 into early 2003 led to pumps that could stop working. Audi recalled them to fit new pumps.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 06V-017 and 07V-375. A stall in traffic is dangerous, so get an open recall done right away.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves causes misfires
issues.sym: Rough idle on cold starts, hesitation, a flashing or steady check engine light and misfire codes.
issues.why: This direct-injection engine sprays fuel past the intake valves instead of over them, so oily deposits bake on and choke airflow over time.
issues.next: Have a shop inspect the intake valves and clean them if deposits are heavy. Do not keep driving with a flashing check engine light.

issues.t: Power trunk lid can drop shut on its own
issues.sym: The open trunk lid sinks or closes by itself, sometimes while someone is loading the trunk.
issues.why: If the gas strut that holds the lid loses pressure, the power lid system could let it close unexpectedly. A recall updates the software.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 07V-334 and replace weak trunk struts. Keep hands and heads clear until it is fixed.

issues.t: Fuel lines in the engine bay can leak
issues.sym: Raw fuel smell from under the hood or inside the car, sometimes with visible wetness on the engine.
issues.why: Several recalls cover fuel leaks on these cars: a fuel line that weakens at a crimp point, an under-hood fuel hose that breaks down, and leaking injection system seals on 2012 cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 17V-781, 16V-646 and 15V-019. If you smell fuel, park outside and have it inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Electric coolant pump can overheat and catch fire
issues.sym: Often no warning. Possible burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, sometimes after the car is parked.
issues.why: The small electric after-run coolant pump can clog with debris or short out from moisture and overheat. A first recall changed software, and a second one replaces the pump.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 17V-002 and 18V-229. If either is open, have it done now and park outside until it is.

issues.t: Front passenger airbag sensor can fail
issues.sym: Airbag warning light on, or the passenger airbag off light showing with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: The sensing mat in the front passenger seat that detects an occupant can wear and stop working, which can switch the passenger airbag off.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 18V-370 and 15V-823. Until it is repaired, have adult passengers ride in the back if the airbag off light is showing.

issues.t: Auxiliary heater connector can overheat
issues.sym: Burning plastic smell from the vents or dash, weak heat on cold mornings, or smoke in rare cases.
issues.why: The electrical connector on the auxiliary cabin heater may not have been fully seated, so it can build heat at the terminals and melt.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 18V-862. If you smell burning from the vents, switch the climate system off and have it inspected right away.

issues.t: Fuel rails can leak
issues.sym: Fuel smell under the hood or in the cabin, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: The left and right fuel rails on the engine can seep fuel. Audi recalled the cars to replace both rails.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 19V-035. Fuel near a hot engine is a fire risk, so park outside and get it fixed promptly.

issues.t: Mild-hybrid starter generator can short out
issues.sym: An electrical system malfunction warning with a battery symbol, the car refusing to restart, or a burning smell or smoke from the engine bay.
issues.why: Moisture can get into the belt-driven starter generator of the mild-hybrid system and short it. Owners also report the same warning when the converter between the high-voltage and 12-volt systems fails.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 20V-153. If the warning appears, pull over safely and have the car towed rather than driving on.

issues.t: Spilled drink in the back seat can shut the car down
issues.sym: After liquid is spilled on the rear seat, a cluster of warning lights appears and the engine can lose power or shut off.
issues.why: A main communication module sits under the rear seat, and liquid soaking through can short it. A recall adds a protective cover.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 22V-861 and keep liquids away from the rear seat cushion until the cover is fitted.

issues.t: Fuel gauge can stick and read wrong
issues.sym: The gauge and range display stop dropping, and the car can run out of fuel while still showing some in the tank.
issues.why: The fuel level sender in the tank can stick in place. A recall fits a new in-tank sensor.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 22V-155. Until then, refuel by mileage rather than by the gauge.

issues.t: Rear suspension lock nut can break
issues.sym: A knock from the rear, the car feeling loose or steering itself from the back, or uneven rear tire wear.
issues.why: The lock nut on the rear trailing arm can crack from corrosion under stress, which lets the rear wheel alignment shift. A follow-up recall rechecks alignment and tires after the first repair.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 21V-295 and 22V-034. If the rear end feels unstable, stop driving and have it towed in.

issues.t: Engine computer fault can stall the engine
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving or will not restart, usually with warning lights.
issues.why: A semiconductor inside the engine control unit can short-circuit on some 2022 cars. Audi recalled them to replace the unit.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 22V-368 and have it done before relying on the car, since a stall can happen without warning.

issues.t: Backup camera image may not appear
issues.sym: The screen stays blank, black or frozen when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Software faults in the infotainment system can stop the camera picture from showing, and on some 2022 cars the main unit itself can be damaged at shut-off. Recalls update the software or replace the unit.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 25V-900, 22V-742 and 22V-806. Until fixed, back up using mirrors and a look over the shoulder.

issues.t: Timing chain tensioner and guides can fail
issues.sym: A rattle or whirring from the back of the engine, loudest for the first seconds after a cold start, sometimes with a check engine light or rough running.
issues.why: The plastic chain guides and the hydraulic tensioners sit at the rear of these engines and wear out. Once a tensioner stops holding pressure the chain goes slack and can jump.
issues.next: Have it looked at right away and avoid long drives. A slack chain can wreck the engine within a few hundred miles, and the repair means pulling the engine out the front of the car.

issues.t: Ignition coils fail and cause misfires
issues.sym: Check engine light, shaking at idle, stumbling under acceleration, sometimes the car dropping into a low-power mode.
issues.why: The individual coil-on-plug units sit in a hot engine bay and break down with age and heat, usually once the car has some years on it.
issues.next: Get the misfire read out and the failed coils replaced. Many owners replace the whole set with plugs at once so the problem does not come back a cylinder at a time.

issues.t: Intake manifold flap motor sticks
issues.sym: Rough, lumpy idle that is worst when the engine is cold, sometimes a check engine light and a flat spot off idle.
issues.why: A small electric motor swings the flaps inside the intake manifold. The gears and the position sensor inside it wear, so the flaps stop moving where the computer expects.
issues.next: Have the fault code read and the motor replaced. It is not dangerous, but a stuck flap keeps the engine running badly and can foul the intake over time.

issues.t: Window regulator breaks and the glass drops
issues.sym: A clunk or grinding from inside the door, the window going down but not back up, or the glass sitting crooked in the frame.
issues.why: The plastic parts and the cable in the window lift mechanism wear and let go, usually in the front doors first.
issues.next: Keep using that window as little as possible and have the regulator replaced when convenient. Tape or prop the glass up if it has dropped so rain does not get in.

issues.t: Side and head airbags may not deploy properly (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing a driver can feel. The airbag warning light may stay off even though the bags are affected.
issues.why: Audi found that the driver, passenger or head airbags in these cars may not inflate the way they should in a crash.
issues.next: Have the car checked against the recall by VIN and the affected airbags replaced. The work is free at an Audi dealer.

issues.t: Rear seat belt may not lock onto a child seat (recall)
issues.sym: The rear belt pulls in and out freely instead of locking when you pull it all the way out to fit a child seat.
issues.why: The automatic locking mode in the rear seat belt retractor may not engage, so a child seat held in by the belt can move in a crash.
issues.next: Stop using that seating position for a child seat until it is fixed, or anchor the seat with the lower latches. The dealer replaces the rear belt assemblies free under the recall.
